items.title: Bank Negara: Most businesses face higher costs, but pass-through remains limited
items.summary: Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said almost 80 per cent of businesses engaged by the central bank had cited higher cost pressures as an issue. "Almost 80 per cent experience higher cost pressure. Abdul Rasheed said demand conditions were influencing businesses' ability to raise prices.

items.title: From fires to landslides, K9 dogs answered 277 calls in 2026
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The Fire and Rescue Department's K9 Unit responded to 277 cases nationwide last year, with Sarawak recording the highest number at 64. Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said Selangor recorded the second-highest number with 39 cases, followed by Perak with 27. He said the unit had four main areas of operation — fire investigation, Urban Disaster Search and Rescue (UDSAR), SAR Cadaver and SAR Wilderness.

items.title: Teo Nie Ching insists Johor DAP won’t dictate, delegates hold Cabinet fate in Sunday congress
items.summary: KULAI, Aug 14 — Johor DAP delegates are free to decide whether the party’s leaders should remain in government posts, including the federal Cabinet, or relinquish those positions while continuing to support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, ahead of the special congress this Sunday. Johor DAP chief Teo Nie Ching said the state leadership is leaving it to more than 400 delegates, who have the freedom to make decisions based on their respective views and understanding of the party’s direction. We give the freedom to the delegates or representatives to make that decision at DAP’s national congress this Sunday.

items.title: Maxis Q2 net profit rises 9.5pct to RM436mil, declares four sen dividend
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Maxis Bhd's net profit rose 9.5 per cent year-on-year to RM436 million in the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 from RM398 million, while revenue increased 3.91 per cent to RM2.66 billion from RM2.56 billion. The mobile operator said the performance was supported by steady service revenue growth of 2.2 per cent to RM2.25 billion, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) rose 2.7 per cent to RM1.12 billion. For the first six months, net profit increased to RM853 million from RM769 million a year earlier, while revenue rose to RM5.39 billion from RM5.17 billion.

items.title: Malaysia’s inflation outlook steady at 1.5–2.5 pc, BNM stresses external pressures remain manageable
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Malaysia’s headline inflation rose to 1.9 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 from 1.6 per cent in the preceding quarter, while core inflation moderated to 1.9 per cent from 2.1 per cent, Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) said today. BNM Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said higher input costs had so far seen limited pass through to consumer prices. The central bank’s figures showed producer cost pressures were concentrated at the upstream stage, with crude materials prices rising 27.5 per cent and intermediate inputs 3.7 per cent, while finished goods prices increased 1.4 per cent.

items.title: Bank Negara expects 5pct GDP growth for 2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia remains confident that Malaysia's economy will grow by around five per cent this year, although growth could come in slightly below or above that level. Bank Negara governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said the economy had continued to perform above expectations over the past three quarters, supported by a broad-based expansion in domestic and external demand. Within exports, both electrical and electronics (E&E) and non-E&E products recorded growth, while the information and communications technology (ICT) services sector also expanded.

items.title: CelcomDigi Q2 net profit falls 9.3pct on higher costs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: CelcomDigi Bhd's net profit fell 9.3 per cent year-on-year to RM398 million in the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, due to increased costs related to 5G network utilisation and net financing. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the group said the initiatives lifted subscriber numbers by 3.8 per cent and 37.2 per cent, respectively, contributing a combined RM61 million to revenue growth. For the first half of 2026, net profit slipped 0.9 per cent to RM816 million from RM823 million a year earlier, while revenue was largely unchanged at RM6.39 billion.

items.title: One year after son attacked, Rafizi decries threats, says case ‘died off’ unresolved
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 14 — After a year since the attack on his child in Putrajaya, Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli has claimed the case has “gone quiet and died off”. “A year has passed, and the case has gone quiet,” he wrote on Facebook, adding that he had been informally told by Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail of a suspected mastermind, but his request for an open statement in Parliament was rejected. Rafizi vowed to continue seeking justice.

items.title: Hadi insists PM should have attended TH RCI parliamentary sitting
items.summary: MARANG: Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim should have attended the special parliamentary sitting on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). He said this would have allowed Anwar to answer questions raised by members of parliament, and that this was appropriate as Anwar had called for the session. he said.

items.title: Affin Bank Q2 net profit falls 11pct on higher impairment allowances
items.summary: Net fee and commission income jumped 60.6 per cent to RM95 million from RM59.16 million. However, net gains on financial instruments fell to RM26.58 million from RM68.61 million, while other income declined to RM41.09 million from RM56.91 million. Pre-tax profit fell 8.1 per cent to RM165.19 million from RM179.82 million.

items.title: Vietjet Thailand to fly to KL from Bangkok on Oct 9
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Vietjet Thailand, the subsidiary of low-cost carrier Vietjet Air, will start flying daily to Kuala Lumpur from Bangkok on Oct 9 using its Boeing B737-8 aircraft. Vietjet Thailand will fly to Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 2 (KLIA T2) from Bangkok Suvarnabhumi Airport. Vietjet Thailand said the new service will also connect travellers from Malaysia to its domestic and international network.

items.title: Loke challenges ECRL to start operations this December
items.summary: GOMBAK: Transport Minister Anthony Loke has challenged Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) and China Communications Construction Company (CCCC) to bring forward the East Coast Rail Link's opening to early December 2026, ahead of the previously targeted January 2027. The System Integration Test and Final Functional Review mark key pre-operational stages for the ECRL, with the Final Functional Review regulated by the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD). He said the ministry was in talks with the Land Public Transport Agency to simplify the Final Functional Review process, which he described as having been rigid.

items.title: CIMB cuts LPI forecasts, target price as underwriting outlook weakens
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd has cut its earnings forecasts for LPI Capital Bhd by 12.1 per cent to 14 per cent for financial years 2026 to 2028 (FY26-FY28). CIMB Securities raised its motor portfolio combined ratio assumption to about 100 per cent for FY26-FY28 from 90 per cent previously, reflecting adverse claims experience. It also lowered its GWP growth forecasts to 6.8 per cent, 6.7 per cent and 6.9 per cent for FY26, FY27 and FY28, respectively, from 8.2 per cent, 8.4 per cent and 7.8 per cent previously.

items.title: Israel reopens West Bank settlement evacuated 20 years ago
items.summary: GANIM, Palestinian Territories: Israel officially reopened the West Bank settlement of Ganim on Thursday, more than 20 years after it withdrew from the community, in a move emblematic of the current government's policy of rapid settlement expansion. We're arriving now," new resident Reut Baran, 35, told AFP in front of her new home. Ganim is one of four Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank that Israel evacuated under former prime minister Ariel Sharon's disengagement plan in 2005.

items.title: Why investors must look beyond the numbers
items.summary: According to KWAP's official clarification, the wider case involved deliberate financial manipulation and misrepresentation of the company's financial reporting. The larger lesson is therefore not simply whether a prescribed process was followed, but whether the evidence underlying an investment has been independently and sufficiently verified. Beyond The Financials Financial due diligence remains indispensable.

items.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill two including senior policeman
items.summary: GAZA CITY: Israeli strikes in Gaza killed two people including a senior police officer on Thursday, health officials said, the second straight day of bombardment after a lull due to a US peace push. Al-Shifa Hospital said it had received the body of Gaza City's police governor Jamal Abu Kamil. Gaza's interior ministry confirmed Abu Kamil "was assassinated in an Israeli airstrike targeting his vehicle on Al-Rashid Street, southwest of Gaza City."

items.title: Makkah defence pact should be viewed in the right context
items.summary: LETTERS: Many analyses of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan begin by asking whether the Muslim world is creating an "Islamic Nato''? If the agreement simply creates another military bloc, the Muslim world is not creating anything fundamentally new. A strategic ummah requires the ability to turn solidarity into capacity, technology, diplomacy, economic influence and strategic leverage.

items.title: Malaysia’s economy expands 6pc in Q2, first‑half growth steady at 5.7pc, says BNM
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, AUG 14 — Malaysia’s economy expanded by 6 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, bringing first-half growth to 5.7 per cent. The services sector grew 5.9 per cent, manufacturing 7.3 per cent, mining and quarrying 9.2 per cent, and construction 6.5 per cent, while agriculture contracted 3.7 per cent. Private consumption increased 4.8 per cent, while private investment rose 4.3 per cent.

items.title: Landfill lunches? Sabah group asks Kota Kinabalu City Hall to clarify packed food claims
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 14 — The Sabah Environment Action Group (SEAG) is seeking a clarification from City Hall (DBKK) over claims that food vendors are selling packed meals at the Kayu Madang landfill. The post, which appeared on the Instagram page sabah.info, suggested that food vendors were selling packed food at the landfill and asked whether anyone wished to place an order. In a statement Thursday, SEAG hoped City Hall could clarify whether this was indeed taking place at the municipal landfill, located in the KKIP area, which serves not only Kota Kinabalu but also neighbouring municipalities, including Petagas, Putatan, Penampang, Tuaran and Kota Belud.

items.title: No time limit on Nurul Izzah's leave, says Fuziah
items.summary: AYER KEROH: PKR has not set a time limit for deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar's leave of absence, which begins next week as she resumes her studies. She said PKR was ready to welcome Nurul Izzah back as deputy president once she was ready to resume her duties. Fuziah said Nurul Izzah would first complete her responsibilities throughout the PKR national congress before beginning her leave.

items.title: Police probe claim 12-year-old boy chased by Hilux in Pasir Gudang
items.summary: "However, the Hilux chased my son and made two rounds while chasing him. Fortunately, a nasi campur trader in front of a house called out to my son," he said. He said the woman asked his son to come closer and sit with her.

items.title: Man held over BMW fire linked to money-lending arrangement in Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A 22-year-old man, believed to be a moneylender's runner, has been remanded for seven days over an attack in which a BMW was set on fire in Air Itam. The remand order was issued by magistrate Noor Idayu Salim and began today to facilitate police investigations under Section 435 of the Penal Code. The suspect is believed to have been paid between RM900 and RM1,000 to set fire to a BMW 220i belonging to a 61-year-old man at Jalan RU3 Air Itam on Aug 8.

items.title: Sarawak plans RM50mil regenerative medicine hub
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sarawak is proposing a RM50 million investment to develop Southeast Asia's first integrated regenerative medicine hub, aimed at bringing research, manufacturing and clinical applications under one roof. The Sarawak Regenerative BioFoundry is a collaboration between Malaysian Bioeconomy Development Corp and BioVerde Technologies Sdn Bhd, the commercial arm of the Sarawak Biodiversity Council. Mohd Khairul said Bioeconomy Corp currently supports biotechnology companies developing more than 50 cell and gene therapy products, providing a potential pipeline for the BioFoundry.

items.title: Magna Prima sets out RM700mil 8 Conlay rehabilitation deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Magna Prima Bhd's proposed restructuring and rehabilitation of the troubled 8 Conlay development involves a commercial entitlement of up to RM700 million, to be satisfied through redeemable secured loan securities (RSLS). In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Magna Prima said the RM700 million represents the agreed commercial allocation arising from the transfer of the development undertaking to Delta 8 Sdn Bhd, the special purpose vehicle set up for the restructuring. The arrangement also involves the assumption of specified liabilities by Magna Prima's wholly owned subsidiary Permata Juang (M) Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Police appeal for information on missing Kajang teenager
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are seeking the public's assistance in locating 17-year-old Farzanah Nabila Abdullah, who was reported missing from Taman Jasmin, Kajang, early yesterday. Kajang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said police received a report concerning the girl's disappearance about 1.20pm yesterday. "Farzanah was believed to have gone missing at 12.20am yesterday, with her last known location recorded at 940, Jalan Jasmin 28, Taman Jasmin, Kajang," he said in a statement.

items.title: In Johor, police probe claim of suspected Toyota Hilux following student walking home
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 14 — Police are investigating a report that a Toyota Hilux followed a food trader’s 12-year-old son as he was walking home in Taman Megah Ria here on Tuesday. Seri Alam police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Sohaimi Ishak today said police were actively investigating the alleged incident involving the primary school pupil, which was reported to have occurred at 4.45pm. “In the report, the boy claimed to be followed by the Toyota Hilux in the Seri Alam area.

items.title: Rafales, Typhoons, Nato jets converge on Subang Air Base
items.summary: SUBANG: Fighter jets, strategic airlifters and aerial tankers from Malaysia, India, Germany, Spain and Nato converged on Subang this week, turning the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) base here into a hive of military air activity. The aircraft are transiting through Subang after participating in Exercise Pitch Black 2026 in Australia, with some also taking part in bilateral training between the RMAF and Indian Air Force (IAF). Also present were Airbus A400M Atlas transport aircraft operated by the German and Spanish air forces.

items.title: #NSTviral: Ford Ranger driver criticised over pedestrian crossing footage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Ford Ranger driver has drawn criticism after dashcam footage appeared to show the vehicle continuing through a pedestrian crossing as several people crossed the road. The vehicle appeared to continue moving as pedestrians made their way across the road. One user, @Eldard Low, commented, "It's really embarrassing."

items.title: Malaysia's inflation rises to 1.9pct in Q2 as fuel costs increase
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's headline inflation rose to 1.9 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, from 1.6 per cent in the first quarter on higher external cost pressures and rising fuel prices. Fuel prices, particularly RON97 and diesel, increased during the quarter, resulting in fuel inflation rising to five per cent compared with a 1.5 per cent decline in the first quarter. Inflation in jewellery and watches moderated to 23.7 per cent, from 39.1 per cent previously, while rent inflation eased to 1.4 per cent from 1.6 per cent.

items.title: [UPDATED] Malaysia's economy grows 6pct in Q2, beats advance estimate [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's economy expanded 6.0 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 (Q2 2026), exceeding the 5.8 per cent advance estimate and accelerating from 5.4 per cent in the first quarter. The stronger performance was supported by resilient domestic spending and solid export growth, with all major economic sectors except agriculture expanding during the quarter, Bank Negara Malaysia said. He said E&E exports remained the key driver, reflecting strong external demand amid the ongoing global technology upcycle.

items.title: Malaysia may one day vote online, EC says trust and security top priorities
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 14 — The Election Commission (EC) has not ruled out the possibility of introducing online or electronic voting in Malaysia in the future. According to Berita Harian (BH), EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said the proposal would however, require thorough study, particularly in terms of public trust and confidence in such a system. “The EC is examining the possibility of implementing e voting before it is introduced in Malaysia.

items.title: Police hunt 2 women over RM16k gold bracelet theft in Terengganu
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: Police are tracking down two women believed to be involved in the theft of a gold bracelet worth about RM16,000 from a jewellery shop at Batu 8, Kampung Batu Enam, Jalan Kelantan, here, yesterday morning. Kuala Terengganu district police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the incident occurred at 10.59am yesterday. He said the theft was discovered when a shop employee conducted a stock check and found that a 916 gold bracelet weighing 28.01g was missing.

items.title: STT GDC secures RM5.6bil financing for Johor data centre campus
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: ST Telemedia Global Data Centres (STT GDC) has secured a green financing facility of up to US$1.37 billion (RM5.6 billion) to support the development of its flagship Malaysian data centre campus in Johor. Through the investment, STT GDC is also committed to building local capabilities, strengthening industry partnerships and operating responsibly as it expands in Johor, said the company in a statement today. STT GDC group chief financial officer Nelson Lim said the financing marked an important milestone in the company's continued investment in Malaysia.

items.title: My son's case has 'gone quiet and died', says Rafizi a year after attack [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former economy minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli claims the investigation into the attack on his son in Putrajaya a year ago has "gone quiet and died". "A year has passed, and the case has simply gone quiet and died," the former Pandan member of parliament said in a video posted on social media. He claimed he was "informally informed" by Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail about a suspected mastermind.

items.title: ECRL on track to start commercial operations by Jan 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) has reached 95.08 per cent overall progress and entered its testing and commissioning phase ahead of commercial operations in January 2027. Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the project remained on schedule for Phase 1 completion in December with the Kota Bharu-Gombak alignment targeted to begin operations in January 2027. Phase 2, connecting Gombak to Port Klang is expected to be completed by December 2027 with operations scheduled to begin in January 2028.

items.title: Pakistani man pleads guilty to robbery, causing hurt over mobile phone
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A Pakistani man pleaded guilty in the Sessions Court here today to robbing and causing hurt to a man over a mobile phone. "Plead guilty," he told the court. Anuarul told the court no bail was offered as the accused was a foreigner.

items.title: Johor DAP delegates free to decide on unity government position
items.summary: KULAI: Johor DAP will give its delegates the freedom to decide whether the party should remain in the unity government at its congress this Sunday. Its chairman, Teo Nie Ching said the party would abide by whatever decision was reached through a vote by delegates at the congress. The deputy communications minister said party leaders were confident that delegates would make the best decision for the future direction of the party and the country.

items.title: No water, no stay: KK hotels hit by cancellations amid supply cuts since Aug 8
items.summary: KOTA KINABLAU, Aug 14 — A water supply disruption in the State Capital has affected 14 hotels since Wednesday (Aug 12), according to the Malaysian Association of Hotels (MAH) Sabah and Labuan Chapter. Its chairman, Suresh Ramasamy, urged the Sabah Water Department to urgently stabilise and restore supply, noting that initial disruptions involving several premises had begun as early as Aug 8. Warning that prolonged multi-day uncertainty could weaken tourism confidence ahead of Visit Malaysia 2026 and Visit Sabah Year 2027, MAH called for priority tanker assistance and clearer restoration timelines for affected premises.

items.title: Paid to remove bad luck, lost a fortune instead: Police say ritual scam cost Sabah victims RM600,000
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 14 — Police have detained 12 people, including seven Chinese women, over an alleged “Chinese-medium” scam linked to losses of about RM600,000. He said the syndicate allegedly offered fortune-telling, traditional treatment and rituals to remove bad luck. Mohd Azhar said four suspects were detained during raids in Kota Kinabalu and Keningau on Saturday, while eight more, including seven Chinese women, were detained in Kota Belud the following day.

items.title: ‘Party within the party’: Nurul Izzah says PKR unity threatened by internal clashes
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 14 — PKR’s deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar has cautioned that the party cannot remain strong if it is distracted by internal disputes. Speaking at the joint Wanita Keadilan and Angkatan Muda Keadilan congress in Ayer Keroh today, she said the party risked weakening itself if factionalism continued to dominate, The Star reported. She said the party could not be strong if its energy continued to be consumed by internal disputes, noting that every hour spent quarrelling among members was time lost in winning public support.

items.title: Sri Muda petrol station brawl sees man slashed with machete, police confirm investigation underway
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 14 — A man was left with serious injuries to his left hand following an alleged machete attack during a fight involving several individuals in Sri Muda yesterday. Shah Alam district police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said officers received a report from the injured man and have since opened investigations. ACP Sarudin urged members of the public with information to assist police by contacting investigating officer Assistant Superintendent Shamsiah Noor Zakaria at 012 830 8706.

items.title: Serian has Malaysia’s worst air quality with API at 183, Kuching and Samarahan tie at 171 while Cheras chokes in the peninsula
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — As of 10am today, 10 locations across Malaysia recorded unhealthy air quality levels, with most of them concentrated in Sarawak. According to data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Serian registered the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 183, followed closely by Kuching (171), Samarahan (171), Sri Aman (163), Sarikei (158), Mukah (152) and Bintulu (147). Meanwhile, 56 locations recorded moderate API levels (51-100), while only two areas registered good air quality (below 50).

items.title: ‘Somebody has to pay’: Serian chief says Sarawakians are fed up with yearly haze from Kalimantan Barat
items.summary: SERIAN, Aug 14 — Serian District Council chairman Dato Peter Minos has voiced his frustration over the worsening haze, saying the town’s iconic mountain view had been “lost in the haze”. He said residents were asking where the mountain range, normally visible from the Serian District Council building, had gone when he was in Serian at 10am on Thursday. According to Minos, Serian was experiencing its worst haze situation in recent years, which he attributed to smoke from Kalimantan Barat, Indonesia, being blown into the area by prevailing winds.

items.title: Valve fault delays water supply recovery for 15,000 Sibu consumers
items.summary: In a statement, Sarawak Water Sdn Bhd said during the restoration process, a 600mm-diameter delivery valve at the Salim Water Treatment Plant experienced an unexpected malfunction, which further affected the recovery of water supply to several areas. Sarawak Water said approximately 15,000 consumers in several areas in Sibu are expected to continue experiencing temporary water supply interruption or low water pressure. Sarawak Water said water supply would be restored progressively, with some areas receiving supply earlier than others depending on their location within the distribution system.

items.title: ‘I will continue saving’: Tabung Haji depositors stand by institution despite RCI spotlight
items.summary: For the majority of Muslims in Malaysia, TH is not merely an ordinary financial, savings and investment institution. “Of course, I will continue saving with TH to ensure that when the time comes, and I am blessed with the opportunity to become a TH haj pilgrim, I will have sufficient savings,” she told Bernama. Muhammad Haikal also said he intended to open TH savings accounts for his three children, aged seven, four and three.

items.title: Police investigate Pasir Mas classroom clash as teacher allegedly hits pupil and mother with cane
items.summary: PASIR MAS, Aug 14 — Police have detained a 54 year old teacher accused of assaulting a pupil and the boy’s mother with a cane in two separate incidents this week. According to Harian Metro , the arrest followed a report lodged by the mother, who alleged her son — a pupil at a primary school in Pasir Mas — was struck by the teacher. The mother raised the matter with the school, prompting the headmaster to arrange a meeting the next day.

items.title: Toyota van driver dead, five passengers injured after collision with lorry on North-South highway near Kluang
items.summary: KLUANG, Aug 14 — A woman was killed while five others were injured in an accident involving a van and a lorry at KM55.1 of the North-South Expressway (PLUS) northbound early this morning. Renggam Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) operations commander Shoromi Salih said five personnel and a Sitrak fire and rescue vehicle were dispatched to the scene, located 51 kilometres away, upon receiving a report. “The driver of the Toyota van, a woman, was confirmed dead at the scene after becoming trapped in the driver’s section,” he said in a statement.

items.title: It’s up to you, parents: Sarawak minister says won’t shut kindergartens, childcare centres even if API is over 200
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 14 — Kindergartens (Tadika) and childcare centres (Taska) in Sarawak may continue operating during the current haze to accommodate children whose parents need to work, said Dato Sri Fatimah Abdullah. “Attendance at Tadika and Taska should remain at the discretion or choice of parents. “These centres are the essential support systems for working parents,” she said in a statement.

items.title: BUDI95 quota too low? PKR Youth wants 300 litres restored, 350 litres for high-mileage users
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 14 — The PKR Youth wing (AMK) wants the monthly Budi Madani RON95 (BUDI95) fuel quota restored to 300 litres and raised to 350 litres for those with high mobility needs, based on clear usage data. AMK chief Muhammad Kamil Ahmad Munim said the call took into account lower global oil prices and the country’s fiscal space, which he said provided room for the government to raise the subsidy quota. “Malay youths must have skills in artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductors, green technology, biotechnology, aerospace, engineering and cybersecurity.

items.title: PKR must look in the mirror, not blame voters, says Youth chief
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 14 — PKR must have the courage to reflect on its performance following recent state elections instead of blaming voters for its defeats, Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) chief Muhammad Kamil Ahmad Munim said. He said while election victories boosted confidence, defeats should instead provide an opportunity for the party to reflect and address its weaknesses, while identifying the reasons why some people remain unconvinced by the party. “The results of the (several) recent state elections must be viewed with courage.

items.title: Haze? Penang schools ready to call off outdoor activities once API crosses 100, shut if over 200
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 14 — Schools in areas recording an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading will be required to suspend all outdoor activities involving students as a precautionary measure amid the haze affecting Penang. “We are monitoring API levels periodically. “Should the API level remain in the ‘unhealthy’ range [this] morning, these schools will suspend all outdoor activities,” he said.

items.title: Heart attack suspected after woman crashes MPV into two parked motorcycles in George Town
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 14 — A woman died after she was believed to have suffered a heart attack while driving a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) this afternoon, before crashing into two motorcycles parked by the roadside along Jalan Macalister here. Northeast district police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said the 36-year-old woman died while receiving treatment at Penang Hospital. “The accident only involved the MPV driver, while the two motorcycles seen in the viral video were unoccupied and parked by the roadside outside a restaurant.

items.title: Anthony Loke’s transport push: LRT3 opens, ridership surges past one million, but congestion fight unfinished
items.summary: Loke said Prasarana was in poor shape when he returned to the ministry in late 2022, with frequent disruptions and maintenance problems affecting public confidence. And I wanted to focus on Prasarana,” he said. he said.

items.title: Uncharted territories: Anthony Loke on alliances, unity constraints and search for lasting model
items.summary: Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, said the political landscape had gone through multiple permutations and collaborations since 2018, with political actors continuing to work out arrangements they believe could strengthen their positions. Loke said political parties and politicians would continue making calculations based on their chances of winning elections and remaining in power. They want to maximise their political function,” he said.

items.title: No tyre marks, no crushed bones: Defence challenges eyewitness accounts in murder trial of senior cop accused of running down teen with Ativa
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 13 — The High Court here today heard that 17-year-old Muhammad Zaharif Affendi Muhd Zamrie was not run over by the vehicle driven by senior police officer DSP Mohd Nazri Abdul Razak, as claimed by eyewitnesses. In his submission at the close of the prosecution’s case before Judge Datuk Bhupindar Singh Gucharan Singh Preet, lead defence counsel M. Athimulan argued that the “run over” theory was inconsistent with objective forensic and medical evidence. He said the medical evidence completely ruled out all probabilities of the ocular evidence (direct oral testimony of an eyewitness) being true and, therefore, the defence counsel team respectfully submitted that the ocular evidence should be rejected.

items.title: ‘I’m still in the Unity Govt’: Lahad Datu MP Yusof Apdal says viral resignation claim ‘untrue and malicious’
items.summary: LAHAD DATU, Aug 13 — Deputy Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Dr Mohammad Yusof Apdal today denied claims that he had resigned and withdrawn from the federal government. In a statement to Bernama today, he said the claim circulating on social media was untrue and malicious. Today, a social media post circulated claiming that Mohammad Yusof had decided to resign as Deputy Minister, effective today.

items.title: RM19,000 in alleged bribes lands Pahang agency official in MACC custody
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 13 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has detained a female official from a government agency in Pahang over allegations of soliciting and receiving around RM19,000 in bribes to help secure tenders and contracts at another agency in the state. Sources said the woman, in her 30s, was detained at about 6.45pm yesterday while giving a statement at the Temerloh MACC office. Meanwhile, Pahang MACC director Mohamad Shukor Mahmud, when contacted, confirmed the arrest and said the case is being investigated under Section 16(a)(B) of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: Space, gas and more: Russia and Malaysia eye new areas to work together
items.summary: VLADIVOSTOK, Aug 13 — Russia sees prospects for a partnership with Malaysia in the space industry, Russian Minister of Science and Higher Education Valery Falkov said on Thursday, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti. Meanwhile, Malaysian Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir said that Russia and Malaysia also have significant opportunities for cooperation in the energy sector, including liquefied natural gas and liquefied petroleum gas. — Bernama-Sputnik/Ria Novosti

items.title: 1MDB strikes a deal to drop its civil suit against former CFO, trial continues for Najib and five others
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) and its former chief financial officer (CFO) Radhi Mohamad have struck a deal today to withdraw the US$5.64 billion civil suit against him, with both parties agreeing to record a consent order in court. “My Lord, I can confirm that the plaintiffs and the sixth defendant would like to record a consent judgment or consent order today. They named former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak, 1MDB’s former finance director Terrence Geh Choh Heng, former executive director Casey Tang Keng Chee, former chief investment officer Vincent Beng Huat Koh, Radhi, former investment director Kelvin Tan Kay Jim, and former chief investment officer Nik Faisal Ariff Kamil, as defendants.

items.title: If it feels like this haze has been here forever, you’re right — and 10 areas in Klang Valley and Sarawak are still recording unhealthy air pollution levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — A total of 10 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today, according to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS). In Sarawak, seven areas recorded unhealthy readings, namely Serian with an API reading of 178, Samarahan (177), Kuching (174), Sri Aman (162), Sarikei (157), Mukah (152) and Sibu (151). Meanwhile, 56 areas recorded API readings at the moderate level, while two areas recorded good readings.
